children: Russia's state subsidy paid to companies importing motor gasoline rose 6.6% month-on-month in August to 44,306 roubles per metric ton ($525), while the payout for diesel jumped 39.3% to 49,995 roubles per ton, according to Reuters calculations based on Russia's Federal Antimonopoly Service agency (FAS) data.
Russia had to turn to fuel imports despite being a longtime net fuel exporter after intensive Ukrainian attacks on its refineries caused gasoline shortages.

In order to support imports, the government introduced in July the so-called "import damper" mechanism, which is a monthly tax rebate that compensates authorized importers for the difference between the landed cost of buying foreign refined products and Russia's lower domestic wholesale benchmark prices for AI-92 gasoline and diesel.
The scheme applies specifically to fuel produced outside the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) and sold within Russia to offset domestic supply shortages.

Russia's seaborne gasoline imports were estimated at around 370,000 tons in August. Assuming all volume was cleared through customs and sold domestically within the month, state budget payouts for imported gasoline are set to reach approximately 16.4 billion roubles in September, according to Reuters calculations.
